questions.evidence:
CLUB RULE: A new weekend activity requires support from more than half of all fifty members. Each member may submit one response. The options are support, oppose, or undecided. Members who do not reply are recorded separately rather than counted as opposing the activity.

FIRST RESULTS: Forty members respond. Eighteen support the proposal, twelve oppose it, and ten are undecided. Ten members have not replied. An early announcement says the proposal has enough support because supporters are the largest group among the three response options.

REVIEW MESSAGE: Being the largest response group is not the same as meeting the rule. The committee asks undecided and missing members for a final answer by Friday. Existing supporters and opponents keep their recorded choices unless they request a correction before the deadline.

For a planning exercise, students consider what would happen if all ten undecided members changed to support while everyone else's response stayed the same. They keep this hypothetical result separate from the actual tally, since the final responses have not arrived yet.
questions.explanation: 相對最多不等於達成全體過半。
options: The largest response category is still below the required support count.

Missing replies must all count as support.
The club has fewer than forty members.
